title: Portfolio
text:
A selection of some of my research and academic projects.


The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains
Master’s Thesis · Leiden University & CBS (Statistics Netherlands) · 2026
How do our connections across family, work, education, and neighbourhoods relate to how much we trust other people? Using the CBS Person Network, a whole-population multilayer network covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents, I developed two individual-level measures of cross-domain embeddedness: multiplexity (whether the same people are connected across multiple domains) and participation evenness (how evenly ties are distributed across domains). A key methodological contribution was an adjusted multiplexity measure that accounts for administrative overlap between family and household registers. These measures were linked to the Social Cohesion and Well-being Survey (2020–2023, \(N\) = 28,483) to examine their association with generalised trust.
 Thesis ·  Conference Abstract



Immigration to Europe: An Interactive Dashboard
EMOS Presentation of Official Statistics · Leiden University · 2025
An interactive Shiny application that visualises immigration patterns across European countries using Eurostat data. The dashboard includes time-series views by country, choropleth maps of immigration counts, and maps showing immigration as a share of the national population. Data were sourced from the Eurostat migration (migr_imm8) and population (demo_pjan) databases, combined with NUTS-0 boundary files for spatial visualisation.
 Live app  Code



Housing Price Statistics in Den Bosch
European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) – Statistical Production Systems · Statistics Netherlands (CBS) & Leiden University · 2025
This project implements a reproducible statistical production pipeline for computing average housing prices in Den Bosch. Using synthetic data from the Dutch buildings register and property sales records, the pipeline follows a five-stage workflow from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, validation, and statistical processing to final output.
 Code



Social Factors Influencing Children’s Pro-Environmental Behaviour
Statistical Consulting Project · Leiden University · 2025
How do social factors influence pro-environmental behaviour in children? Participants (\(N\) = 164) from 13 classrooms across two schools completed an effort-based choice task across self, climate, and prosocial targets. We used generalised linear mixed-effects models to test whether social norm messages influenced how much effort children put into pro-environmental choices, and whether this depended on their social susceptibility and classroom cohesion.

Research Experience

Master’s Thesis Intern — Statistics Netherlands (CBS), 2026

Worked with the CBS Population Network, a whole-population multilayer network of the Netherlands (approximately 17 million residents), linking administrative register data across domains of work, education, household, family, and neighbourhood.
Developed an adjusted multiplexity measure to account for administrative overlap between family and household registers.
Linked the population-scale network to survey data (\(N\) = 28,483) to investigate how the organisation of social ties across domains relates to generalised trust.
Built reproducible R pipelines using data.table, arrow, and DuckDB for large-scale network computation.

title: About me
text:
About me

  
    

    
  
    
     
  
  
    
     
  
  
    
     
  

  
  
Hi! I’m Milena, a quantitative researcher. I am interested in how the contexts people move through, from families and neighbourhoods to schools and labour markets, shape who they become, and how people navigate, reproduce, or break from those conditions. I want to approach these questions by combining complementary data sources, such as population-scale administrative and register data, longitudinal studies, and surveys.
I studied psychology at Maastricht University, where I became most interested in the quantitative side, and in how to measure what we cannot directly observe. I then got a master’s in Statistics and Data Science from Leiden University. For my thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I examined how people’s embeddedness across social domains relates to generalised trust, using a whole-population network of the Netherlands. The social questions inform what I measure, and what I can measure shapes which questions become answerable.
I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen. There, I spent two years working as an au pair caring for three young children, while studying Dutch at KU Leuven. Being part of their daily lives in a context so different from my own made me curious about how our surroundings shape who we become.
In my free time, you’ll find me taking care of my tropical plants, working in the garden, and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
